transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Any time I have to deal with those stronger cleaning chemicals, I either go out of my way to avoid them or push through it while feeling like I can’t stand being there. I work as a janitor, and it has gotten to the point where it's really affecting my job, so my union representative suggested I come see you.
When you are around these chemicals, do you experience repetitive, unwanted thoughts of harm or contamination, or feel driven to perform specific rituals like excessive washing to ease your anxiety?

No, I don't have those kinds of repetitive thoughts of contamination or feel driven to do any rituals or excessive washing. It's just a direct, intense wave of fear and physical panic—like my heart starts pounding and I feel like I can't get a breath—whenever I see or smell those strong chemicals.
How long have you been experiencing this intense fear and avoidance of these cleaning chemicals? Has it been going on for at least six months?
Yes, it has been going on for about two years now, ever since that chemical spill incident happened. So it has definitely been much longer than six months, and it just hasn't gotten any better.
Since that chemical spill, do you experience nightmares, flashbacks, or sudden, upsetting memories of the event itself, even when you aren't around those chemicals?

No, I don't get nightmares, flashbacks, or upsetting memories of the spill when I'm away from the chemicals. The intense fear and panic only hit me when I actually have to deal with them, or even just think about opening one of those supply closets.

Do these sudden feelings of panic, like your heart pounding and trouble breathing, ever happen completely out of the blue, or do they only occur when you are facing or thinking about those cleaning chemicals?

No, they never happen out of the blue. I only get those panic feelings, like my heart pounding and sweaty hands, when I have to face, smell, or even just think about having to deal with those stronger chemicals.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets all criteria for Specific Phobia (F40.2) regarding strong cleaning chemicals. They experience intense, immediate fear and panic symptoms (heart pounding, difficulty breathing, sweaty hands) when exposed to or thinking about the chemicals, and actively avoid them. This has persisted for two years and causes significant occupational impairment. Other diagnoses such as OCD, PTSD, and Panic Disorder were ruled out based on the absence of obsessive-compulsive rituals, intrusive trauma-related re-experiencing, and unexpected panic attacks.
